chunks: And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said:
Concerning a man who performed ẓihār against four women, he said: “Upon him is one expiation.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعِ: four, indicating the number of wives mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: performed ẓihār, declaring a wife unlawful by likening her to a prohibited relative
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: an expiation required for a legal violation
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: one, indicating that only a single expiation is due

ai.seo_question: If a man performs ẓihār against four wives, is one expiation enough or is a separate kaffarah required for each?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on ẓihār involving multiple wives. It states that when a man performs ẓihār with respect to four women, only one kaffarah is due upon him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4843 - In the narration of Ibn Faddal from Ghiyath, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) (peace be upon them), it is reported that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said regarding a man who performed ẓihar (a form of divorce by comparison) against four wives:
"He is obligated to offer only one expiation."
